bio_en: Haji Onnik Avetisian was born in Constantinople on 28 March 1882 to parents who had moved from Van; his teachers included Vardges (Zarmayr), Gnuni and Levon Shant. He grew up during the Bab Ali and Ottoman Bank demonstrations and the Hamidian repression, and was drawn into ARF work. When the 1905 attempt on the Sultan failed and the related Izmir plan was betrayed, he escaped with twelve others by sailboat to the Greek islands, Athens and Alexandria. He later worked through Batum and settled in Urmia, where he kept close to the Caucasian comrades led by Galust Aloyan (Toros).
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Autobiography, truncated at source; death year unknown.
